data.reasoning: The deepseek model successfully reviewed both PKGBUILD and .SRCINFO and found them safe. The package is a standard npm binary package that fetches from the official npm registry with a pinned version and SHA-256 checksum, then copies prebuilt files and creates symlinks. No dangerous operations, network requests, or code execution outside the package scope. The qwen model also found PKGBUILD safe but failed on .SRCINFO due to an API error. The openrouter/free report is advisory-only and had a parsing error. The disagreement stems from technical failures in the audit tool, not actual security concerns.
data.disagreement_analysis: The disagreement was caused by technical failures: qwen encountered an HTTP 400 error when reviewing .SRCINFO, and openrouter/free (advisory-only) had a parsing error on PKGBUILD. The deepseek model successfully reviewed both files and found them safe. The qwen model also successfully reviewed PKGBUILD and found it safe. There is no genuine security disagreement.
coverage_issues: qwen model failed to review .SRCINFO due to API error (HTTP 400 BadRequestError)
openrouter/free model failed to parse PKGBUILD decision (advisory-only report)
learnings: When a model encounters an API error on one file but successfully reviews other files, the tool should not mark the entire audit as inconclusive if other models have successfully reviewed all files
Technical failures (API errors, parsing errors) should be distinguished from security findings - a failed review is not evidence of insecurity
Advisory-only reports with technical errors should not contribute to disagreement calculations
The tool should prioritize successful reviews over failed ones when determining the final verdict
